notes.text: 得る means to obtain/to acquire
notes.html: 得る means to obtain/to acquire

notes.text: [Note negative form is enai えない]
notes.html: [Note negative form is enai えない]

notes.text:
Strictly speaking, the conjugations of 得る are:

- negative: えない

- masu form: えます

- te form: えて

- terminal form (i.e. at the end of sentences, or when attaching to べき): える／うる

- attributive form (i.e. akin to such things as すきな for すき; used when attaching to nouns): うる

- conditional form: うれば



It is the only 二段 (nidan) verb from old Japanese that hasn't fully become an 一段 (ichidan) verb in modern Japanese. (える／うる in old Japanese was う, so it has changed a little already.)



In summary, although うる is a more archaic way of saying える, the only time you can choose between える／うる is when it comes at the end of the sentence, or when attaching to べき (in which case, however, うる is also preferable due to the also archaic nature of べき). This means one should say for example うるために, うるように, うること, うるところ and so on. Additionally, ありうる is never ありえる.



However, in practice, the "wrong" forms are still somewhat often used.

examples.japanese: 考え得る方法は全部試してみたが、どれも失敗に終わった。
examples.body_text:
考え得る方法は全部試してみたが、どれも失敗に終わった。 

		I tried 
		everything I can 
		think of, but everything failed.
examples.body_html:
考え得る方法は全部試してみたが、どれも失敗に終わった。 
I tried everything I can think of, but everything failed.

examples.japanese: そのようなことをしても得るべきものはなにもない。
examples.body_text:
そのようなことをしても得るべきものはなにもない。 

		There is nothing whatever 
		to be gained 
		by resorting to such move.
examples.body_html:
そのようなことをしても得るべきものはなにもない。 
There is nothing whatever to be gained by resorting to such move.

examples.japanese: これらのガスは地球規模の温暖化をもたらし得る。
examples.body_text:
これらのガスは地球規模の温暖化をもたらし得る。 

		These gases 
		can 
		lead to global warming.
examples.body_html:
これらのガスは地球規模の温暖化をもたらし得る。 
These gases can lead to global warming.

examples.japanese: そういう事故は時折起こり得る事だ。
examples.body_text:
そういう事故は時折起こり得る事だ。 

		Such accidents can happen from time to time.
examples.body_html:
そういう事故は時折起こり得る事だ。 
Such accidents can happen from time to time.

examples.japanese: 勤勉さが経験不足を補うこともあり得る。
examples.body_text:
勤勉さが経験不足を補うこともあり得る。 

		Diligence 
		may 
		compensate for lack of experience.
examples.body_html:
勤勉さが経験不足を補うこともあり得る。 
Diligence may compensate for lack of experience.

examples.japanese: 計画を立てる前に、あまり慎重にし過ぎると、計画そのものがひっくり返ることも、時にはあり得るだろう。
examples.body_text:
計画を立てる前に、あまり慎重にし過ぎると、計画そのものがひっくり返ることも、時にはあり得るだろう。 

		Sometimes being overcautious in planning could upset the apple cart.
examples.body_html:
計画を立てる前に、あまり慎重にし過ぎると、計画そのものがひっくり返ることも、時にはあり得るだろう。 
Sometimes being overcautious in planning could upset the apple cart.

examples.japanese: 彼女はオリンピックでメダルを獲得しうる。
examples.body_text:
彼女はオリンピックでメダルを獲得しうる。 

		She 
		can 
		win a medal in the Olympics.
examples.body_html:
彼女はオリンピックでメダルを獲得しうる。 
She can win a medal in the Olympics.

comments.text: Try not to get confused with える (same kanji /generally/ different meaning).
comments.html: Try not to get confused with える (same kanji /generally/ different meaning).

comments.text: A verb-suffix 得る will generally have this meaning and /usually/ be pronounced うる but I hear that it's increasingly common for that usage to /also/ be pronounced える
